transcript.text: theres water in the bottom of my frige under the salad draws, keeps comming back after i mop it up

The most likely cause is a blocked defrost drain. Defrost water should run through a small hole/channel at the bottom of the inside back wall; when it blocks with debris or ice, it overflows into the bottom beneath the salad drawers. 1. Switch the fridge-freezer off and unplug it. Remove the salad drawers and put towels down.
2. Find the small drain hole or channel at the base of the rear wall. Clear visible debris gently with a soft pipe cleaner or cotton bud—do not use a sharp tool.
3. Flush it with small amounts of warm, not boiling, water using a squeezy bottle or turkey baster. If it is frozen solid or will not clear, it may need a full defrost with the appliance switched off and doors open until all ice has melted; then clear and flush the drain. If the drain appears clear but the water returns, the next things to check are the door seal and the drain tube/tray at the back, and an engineer may be needed if the hidden tube is blocked or split.

ok i found a little groove with a hole at the bottom of the back wall and it was full of bits of lettuce and gunk. i cleared it with a cotton bud and then poured warm water down and it went straight down now. the water is only inside the fridge btw, none near the plug or on the kitchen floor. is that it then?

Yes — that is very likely to have been it. The lettuce debris and gunk had blocked the defrost drain, so the water could not escape and collected beneath the salad drawers. The drain is clear again. Dry the bottom of the fridge and keep an eye on it over the next day or two. To help prevent it returning, keep loose veg, leaves and packaging away from that rear drain groove and give it an occasional wipe. If water comes back despite the drain remaining clear, it would then be worth checking the door seal and fridge levelling, but I would expect this clean-out to cure it.
